column1: BLOCKER · v1.0 · build · Launch-screen entry in Info.plist
column2: K-001 · The app declares no launch screen, and Xcode refuses to upload a build to TestFlight without one. Nothing ships until this exists. Info.plist

column1: BLOCKER · v1.0 · build · Diagnostics off by default
column2: K-002 · Developer logging is still switched on, including a log written into iCloud. A public build has to be quiet by default; only the small footer readout is meant to survive. CurlDebug.verbose

column1: v1.0 · ingest · Duplicate detection on the folder path
column2: K-003 · WIRE — Add a book you already own but have since edited, and you get a second copy on the shelf instead of a match. The code that spots this is written and finished; nothing calls it. §5.2. See also K-025

column1: v1.2 · sync · Sidecars are never written
column2: K-004 · WIRE — Your highlights, notes and place are meant to be written beside each book as a small companion file, so they travel with the book and survive a reinstall. The writer is finished and never runs. §9.1 Clause 2

column1: v1.1 · share · Annotation export has no access point
column2: K-005 · WIRE — There is no way to get your highlights and notes out of a book. The exporter is built; it has no button anywhere. §5.3

column1: v1.2 · sync · Recently Active Books stack unused
column2: K-006 · WIRE — A list of the books you have had open recently exists in the code and appears nowhere in the app. §7.1

column1: v1.2 · ingest · OPDS is an island
column2: K-007 · WIRE — Codex can talk to an online book catalogue — browse it, search it, download from it — but nothing in the app opens that door. The whole client is built and unreachable. §2.1–2.4. Its screen is K-043

column1: v1.0 · shelf · Search — shelf and in-book
column2: K-008 · You cannot search anywhere in Codex: not for a book on the shelf, not for a word inside the book you are reading. The largest single absence. §8.4

column1: v1.0 · shelf · Empty-state buttons do nothing
column2: K-009 · The screen you see when you have no books has two buttons that do nothing when tapped. It is the first thing a new reader meets. §12. Same defect as K-030

column1: v1.0 · overall · Reading events (ReadingEventStore)
column2: K-010 · Nothing records when you read or for how long, so the app can never show you a reading history. This one cannot be added later — every day that passes without it is a day that can never be reconstructed. §12.1 / OWED O0. Feeds K-047

column1: v1.0 · render · Margins, gutter, justification
column2: K-011 · You cannot change the page margins, the gap between the two pages, or whether the text is justified. The settings panel exists; these three never moved into it. §2.3

column1: v1.0 · render · Accessibility pass
column2: K-012 · Codex has never been tested with VoiceOver or with large system text. Whatever works today works by accident. §6

column1: v1.0 · render · Dark mode design pass
column2: K-013 · Reading at night works, but was never designed — the frame, the board and the ornaments are placeholders in the dark. Gate 2

column1: v1.0 · render · Run on iPhone once
column2: K-014 · Codex builds for iPhone and has never once been launched on one. Gate 5

column1: v1.0 · reader · Ruling 3 — only user actions write place
column2: K-015 · Your place in a book should move only when you move it. Six of the eleven things that can write it are not you — which is how you come back to the wrong page. Module 7 §3. Same issue as K-054

column1: v1.0 · manual · Manual: stubs + not-yet-implemented
column2: K-016 · The manual describes five things the app does not actually do yet. It ships as the first book on your shelf, so it must not promise what is not there. Round 3 claims A, F, G, H, I

column1: v1.0 · manual · Amend §11 for the manual-on-the-shelf
column2: K-017 · The plan says the manual lives on your shelf as a real book. The directive it belongs to currently forbids exactly that. One of the two has to change. Module 8 §4

column1: v1.1 · reader · Highlight appears only on re-photograph
column2: K-018 · Highlight a passage and the highlight does not appear until the page is photographed again. What was recorded is correct — only the picture lags. Backlog 1

column1: v1.1 · render · Reader-facing curl palette + angle
column2: K-019 · The page-turn's colour and angle are set with developer sliders. A version of those controls fit for a reader was never designed. Backlog 2

column1: v1.1 · reader · Detect an iOS-killed web process
column2: K-020 · If iOS quietly kills the part of the app that draws pages, Readium reloads and says nothing — so Codex carries on believing you are where you were. Backlog 3

column1: v1.1 · formats · CBZ / comics
column2: K-021 · Comic-book archives (CBZ) cannot be opened. The parser underneath already handles the format; nothing above it does. Backlog 4

column1: v1.1 · formats · PDF, scroll-only spike
column2: K-022 · PDFs cannot be opened at all, including the ones you have that will not convert to epub. Backlog 5

column1: v1.1 · reader · Render thread for the curl
column2: K-023 · A proposal to move the page-turn animation onto its own thread. Parked deliberately: the evidence said it was the wrong cure for the stutter. Backlog 6

column1: v1.1 · shelf · Bookshelf performance (covers, indexer)
column2: K-024 · Every cover is decoded from scratch each time the shelf draws, and nothing is remembered between times. On a large shelf, that is the slowness you feel. Backlog 7

column1: v1.1 · ingest · The same book, edited — merge prompt
column2: K-025 · Add an edited copy of a book you already have and Codex should ask whether to merge the two — which needs your ruling on what a merge keeps. Backlog 8. Detection is K-003

column1: v1.1 · shelf · CoverFlow browser + See all
column2: K-026 · A browse-by-cover view of the shelf, and the See all route into it. Both buttons were taken out when it was deferred. Backlog 9

column1: v1.1 · shelf · Bulk select
column2: K-027 · You cannot select several books at once, so deleting or sharing more than one means doing it one at a time. §9.1–9.3

column1: v1.1 · shelf · Context menu on long press
column2: K-028 · Long-pressing a book on the shelf does nothing. §10

column1: v1.1 · shelf · Ghost record "Remove"
column2: K-029 · When a book's file goes away its record stays on the shelf, and there is no way to erase it. §7

column1: v1.1 · shelf · Book Detail placeholder buttons
column2: K-030 · A book's detail screen has three buttons that do nothing: File…, Force Re-upload, Reset Progress. §11. Same defect as K-009

column1: v1.1 · render · Inline image lightbox
column2: K-031 · Tapping a picture inside a book does nothing — it cannot be opened larger. Fully specified, no code written. 01.1 §A1

column1: v1.1 · render · Font catalogue from the device
column2: K-032 · The typography panel offers a fixed list of fonts written into the app. The fonts actually installed on your iPad are never consulted. §2.4

column1: v1.1 · render · Advanced settings
column2: K-033 · A planned second layer of the settings panel, for controls that should not face a reader. §4.5

column1: v1.1 · render · "More" menu in reader chrome
column2: K-034 · A planned More menu in the reader's chrome. Nothing behind it yet. §4.7

column1: v1.1 · ingest · Keep on device / keep local only
column2: K-035 · No way to tell Codex to keep a particular book on the iPad rather than let iCloud reclaim the space. §8.3, §8.5

column1: v1.1 · ingest · Manual file replacement, batch recovery
column2: K-036 · No way to point a shelf record at a replacement file, and no way to recover a batch of books that failed to come in. §8.4, §8.6

column1: v1.1 · ingest · "Still downloading" on the open path
column2: K-037 · Tap a book iCloud has not finished downloading and the app simply waits, with nothing on screen to say so. The manual already promises it tells you. §8.2

column1: v1.1 · manual · Open the Manual (Settings › About)
column2: K-038 · Once you have closed the manual there is no way to open it again — no entry in Settings, nowhere else either. Ruled, never built. Module 8 §5a

column1: v1.1 · manual · Restore the manual on an empty folder
column2: K-039 · If your book folder is empty the manual should reappear in it. Ruled, never built. Module 8 §5.2

column1: v1.2 · sync · Field encryption (§9.1) before any sync
column2: K-040 · Before anything syncs to iCloud, the private parts of it have to be encrypted. This cannot be added afterwards — anything already synced in the clear stays that way. Ships with K-004 or not at all

column1: v1.2 · sync · CloudKit sync — Module 4 entire
column2: K-041 · Your books, places and notes do not travel between devices at all. The whole of Module 4. Gated on K-040 and K-004

column1: v1.2 · reader · Reading place as selector + words
column2: K-042 · Your place is remembered as a rough position in the file. Remembering the actual sentence instead would survive a font change, a re-flow, or a different device. Module 7 §6

column1: v1.2 · ingest · OPDS browser + Sources tab
column2: K-043 · The screen for browsing an online catalogue, and the Sources tab that reaches it. §2.3, §13. The client behind it is already built: K-007

column1: v1.2 · ingest · Genre, from OPDS tags by book id
column2: K-044 · Books have no genre. Catalogue servers carry genre tags and can supply them later; a book that never came from one falls back to whatever the epub itself declares.

column1: v1.2 · sync · Follow Me / Stay Here, quick switch
column2: K-045 · With two devices, no way to say follow my place or leave me where I am, and no quick way to switch between them. §7.2–7.4

column1: v1.2 · sync · Finished? prompt surfaced
column2: K-046 · Codex can tell when you have finished a book, and never asks. The detection is built; the question is not. §13

column1: v2 · overall · Annual reading report UI
column2: K-047 · A year-in-reading summary. The events it would be built from are K-010, which is v1.0 — this is not. §12.1

column1: v2 · overall · Reading focus / kiosk mode
column2: K-048 · A mode that locks the iPad to reading and nothing else. §12.2

column1: v2 · sync · Apple Intelligence assist
column2: K-049 · Some use of on-device intelligence, not yet specified. §7.5

column1: v2 · share · Codex-to-Codex direct transfer
column2: K-050 · Sending a book straight to another Codex nearby, with no file in between.

column1: v1.0 · render · §3 describes a Core Image compositor
column2: K-051 · DRIFT — The rendering directive describes a page-turn built on Core Image. The app builds it on Readium, a screenshot and Metal instead. The document was never updated; the code is almost certainly the right one. §3

column1: v1.0 · ingest · Two ingestion paths, one live
column2: K-052 · DRIFT — Two separate routes for getting a book into the library exist in the code, and only one of them runs. The other is left over from before folder-as-shelf.

column1: v1.0 · shelf · §8.3 Collections vs folder-as-shelf
column2: K-053 · DRIFT — The directive describes Collections you make yourself. The app uses iCloud folders as shelves instead, and the Collections code sits unused. One of the two should go. §8.3

column1: v1.0 · reader · Module 7 Ruling 3 not enforced
column2: K-054 · DRIFT — The same issue as K-015, from the documents' side: Module 7 states a rule about your reading place that the code does not follow.

column1: v1.1 · docs · Undirected subsystems
column2: K-055 · DRIFT — Five working parts of the reader were never written down as a design, only described in the daily log. Nothing is broken; but if one needs changing, there is no spec to check it against. HANDOFF §13.x

column1: v1.0 · docs · BookContentBlocker has no directive
column2: K-056 · DRIFT — Codex stops books from calling out to the internet, and the manual promises exactly that. The promise is specified nowhere but a single ledger entry. HANDOFF §13.70
